s1.syndrome_frame: Progressive orbital and nasal cavity symptoms with a mass lesion
salient_findings: Nasal mass at the level of the left middle turbinate
Expansile soft-tissue mass in the anterosuperior nasal cavity
key_facts: 4-month history of symptoms
Left eye proptosis
Diplopia
Chemosis
No epistaxis
No headache
No nasal obstruction
Mass at the level of the left middle turbinate
Erosion of the upper nasal septum
Mild left proptosis with full extraocular movements
Normal visual acuity
Expansile, mildly enhancing soft-tissue mass on CT
Remodeling of the left medial orbital wall
Extension to the level of the cribriform plate
Retention of secretions in the left frontal sinus
No dural enhancement or intracranial extension on MRI

shortlist.label: Esthesioneuroblastoma
shortlist.why_kept: Mass in the nasal cavity with extension to the cribriform plate and orbital cavity, consistent with esthesioneuroblastoma

shortlist.label: Inverted papilloma
shortlist.why_kept: Expansile, mildly enhancing soft-tissue mass in the anterosuperior nasal cavity, a common location for inverted papilloma

shortlist.label: Squamous cell carcinoma
shortlist.why_kept: Destructive mass in the nasal cavity with erosion of the upper nasal septum, a possible presentation of squamous cell carcinoma

shortlist.label: Sinonasal undifferentiated carcinoma
shortlist.why_kept: Aggressive mass with destruction of the anterior skull base and erosion of the left lamina papyracea, consistent with sinonasal undifferentiated carcinoma

shortlist.label: Olfactory neuroblastoma
shortlist.why_kept: Mass in the nasal cavity with extension to the cribriform plate, a common location for olfactory neuroblastoma

raw.rationale: The patient's presentation with proptosis, diplopia, and chemosis, along with the imaging findings of an expansile, mildly enhancing soft-tissue mass in the anterosuperior nasal cavity with extension to the level of the cribriform plate, is consistent with esthesioneuroblastoma, a rare malignant tumor originating from the olfactory epithelium.

rejected.label: Inverted papilloma
rejected.why: Inverted papilloma is typically a benign tumor and less likely to cause such extensive destruction and orbital involvement.

rejected.label: Squamous cell carcinoma
rejected.why: Squamous cell carcinoma is more commonly associated with a history of smoking and would likely present with more aggressive features and possibly cervical lymphadenopathy.

rejected.label: Sinonasal undifferentiated carcinoma
rejected.why: Sinonasal undifferentiated carcinoma is a highly aggressive tumor with a poor prognosis, and the clinical presentation and imaging findings do not fully align with this diagnosis.

rejected.label: Olfactory neuroblastoma
rejected.why: Olfactory neuroblastoma is another term for esthesioneuroblastoma, so it is essentially the same diagnosis as the chosen champion.
